gap: No result ChatGPT got states that named reviewers measured the 13.3-inch Mobile Pixels Duex Plus at 152 nits (Parkablogs) and about 200 nits (MBReviews) against the 300 nits Mobile Pixels claims, with 68% sRGB coverage and about 5 W drawn from the laptop.
standout_why: Compared against itechguides.com (cited in both chats), lbdsoftware.com (cited) and Macworld (top result). All three give brightness, weight and gamut only as maker or listing specs: itechguides calls the Duex Plus DS '300-nit class', lbdsoftware prints 'rated' figures and an unsourced '10 to 15 watts', and Macworld's Mobile Pixels figures are spec lists. None names a measurer. techpp.com (cited in chat 2) returned HTTP 403, so it was not compared. The limit on this finding: both measurements are of the 2021-22 Duex Plus, not the current Duex Plus DS, and I found no instrumented review of the DS, the Duex Max DS, or the FOPO S1/S7.
decides: It confirms the size match and qualifies the screen quality; it does not change the pick. Parkablogs ran the 13.3-inch Duex Plus on a 13.3-inch M1 MacBook Air and found the two almost the same size, at 1.3 lb, which supports a 13.3-inch single-screen slider for a 13-inch laptop. The measured 152–200 nits and 68% sRGB mean the page should describe it as an office and document screen, visibly dimmer than the laptop's own panel, not as a 300-nit match. Notebookcheck's FOPO measurement (193 cd/m² peak, 247:1 contrast, hinges that 'teeter') is for a 12-inch 2022 model, so it is only a caution about clip-on dual extenders in general, not evidence about the FOPO S1 or S7 we link. No measurement was found for any product we link.
